title: Affine local domain model of a missing image point
statement: Let $g:U\to Y$ be a finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $y\in\overline{g(|U|)}\setminus g(|U|)$, where closure is in the Zariski topology. There exist $x\in U$, affine open neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ of $y$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq g^{-1}V$ of $x$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and a finite-type ring homomorphism $\varphi:B\to C$ inducing $g|_W$, with $B$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], such that the following hold. The point $z=g(x)\in V$ specializes to $y$ and is distinct from $y$. If $\mathfrak p\subset B$ represents $y$, $\mathfrak r\subset C$ represents $x$, and $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak r)$ represents $z$, then $\mathfrak q\subsetneqq\mathfrak p$. Put $L=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, $h:B\xrightarrow{\varphi}C\to L$, and $R=(B/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. One has $\ker h=\mathfrak q$, and the formula $\iota((b+\mathfrak q)/(s+\mathfrak q))=h(b)/h(s)$, for $b\in B$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p$, defines an embedding $R\hookrightarrow L$ factoring $h$. The ring $R$ is a nonzero Noetherian local integral domain which is not a field, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R=(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q)R$, whose inverse image in $B$ is $\mathfrak p$. The subfield of $L$ consisting of quotients of elements of $R$ identifies canonically, compatibly with $h$, with $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; hence it is $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Here an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors, and $\kappa(\mathfrak a)=D_{\mathfrak a}/\mathfrak aD_{\mathfrak a}$ for a prime $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $D$.

source.place: Tag 0CM2, limits-lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian, proof through the image of the local ring in the source residue field; explicit affine-coordinate expansion, returned steps 1-3.

proof.text: Finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sc-picard-closure-specialization] to $g$ and the given closure point to obtain $x\in U$ with $z=g(x)$ specializing to $y$. Since $y$ is outside the image, $z\ne y$. Choose $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $y$ from the Noetherian affine covering in [pqf-def-locnoeth], so $B$ is Noetherian. Every open containing a specialization contains its generalization: otherwise its closed complement would contain the generalization and its closure. Thus $z\in V$. The affine covering in the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] supplies $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq g^{-1}V$ containing $x$, with finite-type coordinate map $\varphi:B\to C$ inducing $g|_W$.

source.place: Tag 0CM2, limits-lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian, first paragraph of proof; specialization from Tag 02JQ, morphisms-lemma-reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image; affine coverings from the definitions.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak r$ represent $y,x$ in these charts. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] identifies the prime of $z$ with $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak r)$. In a spectrum the closure of $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$: a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Consequently specialization to $\mathfrak p$ gives $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$; equality would give $z=y$. Hence $\mathfrak q\subsetneqq\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 01HY, schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes; Zariski closed sets as in Algebra Tag 00E0, algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology.

proof.text: For $L=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ and $h:B\to C\to L$, clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra], applied to $C,\mathfrak r$, gives $h(b)=0$ exactly when $\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak r$, that is, $b\in\mathfrak q$. Thus $h$ induces an injective map $\bar h:A=B/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow L$. In particular $A$ is a nonzero domain. The ideal $P=\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q$ is proper and prime: products of classes lie in $P$ exactly when the corresponding product in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak p$, so one factor lies there. It is nonzero by the strict inclusion. Set $R=A_P$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, algebra-definition-localization, fraction formulas; explicit expansion of the image ring in Tag 0CM2.

proof.text: Write $M=PR$. Every fraction with numerator outside $P$ is a unit, since the reversed fraction is its inverse. Every fraction with numerator in $P$ lies in $M$. Such a fraction cannot be a unit: an equation $(a/s)(b/t)=1$ would give $ab=st$ in the domain $A$, impossible when $a\in P$ and $s,t\notin P$. Also $M$ consists exactly of fractions with numerator in $P$: sums of such fractions still have numerator in $P$, and multiplication preserves this condition. Thus $M$ is proper and consists of all nonunits; every proper ideal is contained in $M$, and any larger ideal contains a unit. Hence $M$ is the unique maximal ideal. Its inverse image under $B\to R$ is $\mathfrak p$ by the numerator criterion. Choose $a\in P\setminus\{0\}$; its image $a/1$ is nonzero by step 4 and is a nonunit. So $R$ is not a field.

source.place: Tag 07BH, algebra-section-local, paragraph on the maximal ideal of a prime localization; explicit fraction verification.

proof.text: Noetherianity can be checked directly from [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For an ideal $J\subseteq A=B/\mathfrak q$, its inverse image in $B$ has finite generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$; their classes generate $J$, since every element of $J$ lifts to that inverse image. Hence $A$ is Noetherian. For an ideal $H\subseteq R$, put $I=\{a\in A:a/1\in H\}$. Choose finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ of $I$. If $a/s\in H$ then $a/1=(s/1)(a/s)\in H$, so $a\in I$; expanding $a$ in those generators shows that $a/s$ is generated in $R$ by $a_i/1$. Conversely these generators belong to $H$. Therefore every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 00FN, algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence, first two sentences of proof (quotients and localizations).

proof.text: Use the embeddings $A\subseteq R\subseteq L$ just constructed. The quotients of elements of $R$ in $L$ form a subfield: the usual common-denominator formulas give closure under addition and multiplication, and a nonzero quotient $r/t$ has inverse $t/r$. Since every element of $R$ has the form $a/s$ with $a,s\in A$ and $s\ne0$, a quotient of two elements of $R$ is $(a/s)/(b/t)=at/(sb)$ with nonzero denominator. Conversely every quotient $a/b$ of elements of $A$ is also a quotient of elements of $R$. Hence this subfield is exactly the field of fractions of $A$ and of $R$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra], applied to $B,\mathfrak q$, identifies it canonically with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$: send the fraction of $a,b\in A$ to $\bar h(a)/\bar h(b)$. Cross multiplication makes this independent of representatives; every such fraction occurs. On $B$ the map is $h$, proving the requested compatibility.
